4.0.s.en: 1. Completion of the genealogies of Judah

4.0.0.en: 1 The sons of Judah; Pharez, Hezron, and Carmi, and Hur, and Shobal. 2 And Reaiah the son of Shobal begat Jahath; and Jahath begat Ahumai, and Lahad. These are the families of the Zorathites. 3 And these were of the father of Etam; Jezreel, and Ishma, and Idbash: and the name of their sister was Hazelelponi: 4 And Penuel the father of Gedor, and Ezer the father of Hushah. These are the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephratah, the father of Bethlehem. 5 And Ashur the father of Tekoa had two wives, Helah and Naarah. 6 And Naarah bare him Ahuzam, and Hepher, and Temeni, and Haahashtari. These were the sons of Naarah. 7 And the sons of Helah were, Zereth, and Zohar, and Ethnan. 8 And Coz begat Anub, and Zobebah, and the families of Aharhel the son of Harum. 9 And Jabez was more honorable than his brethren: and his mother called his name Jabez, saying, Because I bare him with sorrow. 10 And Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed, and enlarge my coast, and that thine hand might be with me, and that thou wouldest keep me from evil, that it may not grieve me! And God granted him that which he requested. 11 And Chelub the brother of Shuah begat Mehir, which was the father of Eshton. 12 And Eshton begat Bethrapha, and Paseah, and Tehinnah the father of Irnahash. These are the men of Rechah. 13 And the sons of Kenaz; Othniel, and Seraiah: and the sons of Othniel; Hathath. 14 And Meonothai begat Ophrah: and Seraiah begat Joab, the father of the valley of craftsmen; for they were craftsmen. 15 And the sons of Caleb the son of Jephunneh; Iru, Elah, and Naam: and the sons of Elah, even Kenaz. 16 And the sons of Jehaleleel; Ziph, and Ziphah, Tiria, and Asareel. 17 And the sons of Ezra were, Jether, and Mered, and Epher, and Jalon: and she bare Miriam, and Shammai, and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa. 18 And his wife Jehudijah bare Jered the father of Gedor, and Heber the father of Socho, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah. And these are the sons of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh, which Mered took. 19 And the sons of his wife Hodiah the sister of Naham, the father of Keilah the Garmite, and Eshtemoa the Maachathite. 20 And the sons of Shimon were, Amnon, and Rinnah the son of Hanan, and Tilon. And the sons of Ishi were, Zoheth, and Benzoheth. 21 The sons of Shelah the son of Judah were, Er the father of Lecah, and Laadah the father of Mareshah, and the families of the house of them that wrought fine linen, of the house of Ashbea, 22 And Jokim, and the men of Chozeba, and Joash, and Saraph, who had the dominion in Moab, and Jashubilehem. And these are ancient things. 23 These were the potters and the inhabitants of Netaim and Gederah: there they dwelt with the king for his work.

4.0.1.en: The sons of Judah; Pharez, Hezron, and Carmi, and Hur, and Shobal. [1]

4.0.2.en: Pharez was the son of Judah, and Hezron the son of Pharez (1 Chr 2:5); as for the Carmi mentioned here, he is Chelubai (1 Chr 2:9), and he is distinct from the Carmi mentioned in (1 Chr 2:7) and in (Josh 7:1); he was a son of Hezron.

4.0.4.en: Hezron: a Hebrew name meaning "siege or enclosure."

4.0.5.en: Carmi: a Hebrew name meaning "worker in vineyards."

4.0.6.en: Hur: it is thought to be an Egyptian name, taken from the name of the god "Horus."

4.0.7.en: Shobal: the son of Hur, of the house of Caleb, of the tribe of Judah, of the family of Hezron. From his descendants came the inhabitants of the village of Kirjath-jearim (1 Chr 4:2, 4).

4.1.0.en: And Reaiah the son of Shobal begat Jahath; and Jahath begat Ahumai, and Lahad.

4.1.1.en: These are the families of the Zorathites. [2]

4.1.2.en: Reaiah: it is thought that he is Haroeh (1 Chr 2:52), and the meaning is "the seer" or "Yahweh sees."

4.1.3.en: The Zorathites: Zorah was in the south of Judah on the border of the Philistines.

4.1.4.en: Jahath: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "he seizes." Two persons bore this same name: 1. A man of the tribe of Judah, of the family of Hezron (1 Chr 4:2). 2. A Levite, a Kohathite of the house of Izhar in the days of David (1 Chr 24:22).

4.1.5.en: Ahumai: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "Ahuma," and he was one of the heads of the clans of Judah.

4.1.6.en: Lahad: a Hebrew name meaning "load" or "burden," and he is a son of Jahath, of the descendants of Judah.

4.2.0.en: And these were of the father of Etam;

4.2.1.en: Jezreel, and Ishma, and Idbash: and the name of their sister was Hazelelponi: [3]

4.2.2.en: Etam: a Hebrew name meaning "lair of birds of prey." By the father of Etam is meant the builder of the city of Etam. It is the name of more than one city: 1. A town in Judea near Bethlehem, which Rehoboam fortified after the division between the tribes (2 Chr 11:6). Today it is called Khirbet al-Khokh at Solomon's Pool. Traces of water cisterns were found there, and the pools of Solomon near the village of Artas and Ain Etan. 2. A town in the southern part of Judea, which passed from the sons of Judah to Simeon (1 Chr 4:32). Perhaps it is present-day Aitun, eleven miles southwest of al-Khalil.

4.2.3.en: Jezreel: a Hebrew name meaning "God sows," and he is a man of the descendants of Judah [3].

4.2.4.en: Ishma: a Hebrew name, perhaps an abbreviation of the word Ishmael, and he is a man of Judah, the son of Hur.

4.2.5.en: Idbash: a Hebrew name meaning "sweet as honey," and he is a son of the father of Etam, a man of Judah.

4.2.6.en: Hazelelponi: a Hebrew name meaning "He gives shade upon me," the name of a girl of the sons of Judah. The names of some of her brothers, the men, are mentioned.

4.3.0.en: And Penuel the father of Gedor, and Ezer the father of Hushah.

4.3.1.en: These are the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephratah, the father of Bethlehem. [4]

4.3.2.en: Penuel: a Hebrew name meaning "face of God." It is the name of a man of Judah, the father of the inhabitants of Gedor.

4.3.3.en: Gedor: a Hebrew name meaning "fortress" or "walled place." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. A son of Penuel (1 Chr 4:4). 2. A son of Jered by his Jewish wife (1 Chr 4:18).

4.3.4.en: There is also a place called Gedor between Seir and Judah, perhaps within the borders of the tribe of Simeon near the northwestern border of Palestine (1 Chr 4:39), and it appears in the Septuagint as "Gerar."

4.3.5.en: Ezer the father of Hushah: Ezer, a Hebrew name meaning "help." Of the descendants of Judah, from among Hadar.

4.3.7.en: By his saying "the father of Bethlehem," he means its chief.

4.4.0.en: And Ashur the father of Tekoa had two wives, Helah and Naarah. [5]

4.4.1.en: Ashur the father of Tekoa: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "blackness."

4.4.2.en: Helah: a Hebrew name meaning "ornament, adornment, necklace, collar." One of the two wives of Ashur, the ancestor of the men of Tekoa, of the tribe of Judah.

4.4.3.en: Naarah: a Hebrew name meaning "girl," one of the two wives of Ashur and the mother of Ahuzam and his brothers.

4.5.0.en: And Naarah bare him Ahuzam, and Hepher, and Temeni, and Haahashtari. These were the sons of Naarah. [6]

4.5.1.en: Ahuzam: a Hebrew name meaning "the king or the owner," a son of Ashur of the clan of Hezron.

4.5.2.en: Hepher: a Hebrew name meaning "pit or well," of Judah, a son of Ashur of the clan of Hezron in the tribe of Judah.

4.5.3.en: Haahashtari: perhaps from Persian, meaning "follower of the queen," and he is a son of Ashur.

4.6.0.en: And the sons of Helah were, Zereth, and Zohar, and Ethnan. [7]

4.6.1.en: Zereth: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "splendor."

4.6.2.en: Zohar: a Hebrew name meaning "white," and it also appears in the form "Jezoar."

4.7.0.en: And Coz begat Anub, and Zobebah, and the families of Aharhel the son of Harum. [8]

4.7.1.en: Coz: a Hebrew name meaning "thorn," perhaps he was one of the sons of Helah.

4.7.2.en: Anub: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "bound," a son of Coz, one of the chiefs of Judah.

4.7.3.en: Zobebah: a Hebrew name meaning "hatred, anger," and he is a son of Coz, of the sons of Helah.

4.7.4.en: Aharhel the son of Harum: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "brother of Rachel" or "the last of strength." He is the son of Harum, and he was head of a clan in Judah.

4.8.0.en: And Jabez was more honorable than his brethren:

4.8.1.en: and his mother called his name Jabez, saying, "Because I bare him with sorrow." [9]

4.9.0.en: And Jabez called on the God of Israel:

4.9.1.en: "Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed, and enlarge my coast, and that thine hand might be with me, and that thou wouldest keep me from evil, that it may not grieve me!"

4.9.2.en: And God granted him that which he requested. [10]

4.9.3.en: Jabez: a Hebrew name meaning "he causes pain," the name of a man of Judah whom his mother called Jabez because she bore him in pain.

4.9.4.en: His father's name is not mentioned, nor in what age he lived, but it was said of him that he was more honorable than his brethren. All we know about him, whether from the Bible or from Jewish tradition, is that he was a teacher of the Law, Doctor in Law, and that he was a godly man. For this reason the city where he lived was often called by his name (1 Chr 2:55). He was a man of faith, "but without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him" (Heb 11:6).

4.9.5.en: He was called "more honorable than his brethren"; the secret of his greatness and nobility is not that he performed a heroic deed more than his brothers, but that he made God the center of his life and work. He knew how to give God His right place in his life as the Lord, the giver of blessings, the giver of inner victory, the leader of life, and the true fortress against evil.

4.9.6.en: Sorrow no longer has a place in the heart of the man of God, for he knew what to ask, and God granted him what he asked.

4.9.7.en: The prayer of Jabez is regarded as unique, for the prayer, together with its answer, did not occupy more than one verse. He presents to us an ideal prayer accepted before God; he asked and received from God. It was answered quickly, so what is the secret of its acceptance?

4.9.8.en: His prayer included four matters, and revealed the role of God in the life of the believer:

4.9.9.en: The first petition: asking for blessing = the blessed, heavenly life. "Oh that thou wouldest bless me!" means: give me true happiness. God is the giver of blessings and true happiness. The second petition: asking for the enlargement of the border = the widening of the heart in love for God and people. He asks for an enlarged heart in which every person finds a place by love. God is the giver of true love.

4.9.10.en: The third petition: asking that the hand of God be with him = the enjoyment of the divine presence; he longs that He dwell in us, and work in us and through us and protect us. May the hand of God be with us! He asks for the protection of God and His care for him.

4.9.11.en: The fourth petition: asking to be kept from evil = victory over the devil and evil. Being kept from evil: He gives him authority over Satan and all his powers, and thereby removes from him the evil that robs him of his joy in the Lord.

4.9.12.en: Since the petitions came according to the will of God, or the vow that Jabez made, it was said: "And God granted him that which he requested" (1 Chr 4:10). It is stated in the Book of Jeremiah: "Then shall ye call upon me, and ye shall go and pray unto me, and I will hearken unto you. And ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart" (Jer 29:12-13).

4.9.13.en: Jabez became successful in all aspects of his life: in his works and studies and his relationship with others, and his struggle with the pagans. God was always ready to listen to all that was in his heart or mind.

4.10.0.en: And Chelub the brother of Shuah begat Mehir, which was the father of Eshton. [11]

4.10.1.en: Chelub: a Hebrew name meaning "basket or cage for birds," the name of the brother of Shuah. His lineage was not fully known, but he was reckoned among the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 4:11).

4.10.2.en: Shuah: a Hebrew name meaning "low," a man of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 4:11).

4.10.3.en: Mehir: a Hebrew name meaning "price," a man of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 4:11).

4.10.4.en: Eshton: the meaning of the name is not known with certainty. It is the name of one of the sons of Mehir of the tribe of Judah.

4.11.0.en: And Eshton begat Bethrapha, and Paseah, and Tehinnah the father of Irnahash.

4.11.1.en: These are the men of Rechah. [12]

4.11.2.en: Rapha: a Hebrew name meaning "he healed, that is, God healed." Bethrapha: it was built by the son of Eshton.

4.11.3.en: Paseah: a Hebrew name meaning "lame," a man of Judah of the descendants of Chelub (1 Chr 4:12).

4.11.4.en: Tehinnah: a Hebrew name meaning "grace or supplication," of the tribe of Judah, the founder of the city of Nahash, and called its father; he is the son of Eshton (1 Chr 4:12).

4.11.5.en: Nahash: a Semitic name meaning "serpent or snake."

4.11.6.en: Rechah: a place in the portion of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 4:12).

4.12.0.en: And the sons of Kenaz; Othniel, and Seraiah: and the sons of Othniel; Hathath. [13]

4.12.1.en: Othniel: a Hebrew name meaning "God is strength," and it also means "the answering of the Lord," and also "the time of God for myself." Of the descendants of Kenaz, that is, of the clan of the Kenezites, and his father is Jephunneh. He is the younger brother of Caleb (Josh 15:17). The first of the judges of Israel, he reformed the affairs of the people and brought about peace in the country (Judg 1:9-15; 3:5-11).

4.12.2.en: It was said of him: "And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kirjathsepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife. And Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife" (Judg 1:12-13).

4.12.3.en: "And when the children of Israel cried unto the LORD, the LORD raised up a deliverer to the children of Israel, who delivered them, even Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother. And the Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel, and went out to war: and the LORD delivered Chushanrishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand; and his hand prevailed against Chushanrishathaim. And the land had rest forty years. And Othniel the son of Kenaz died" (Judg 3:9-11).

4.12.4.en: We have previously commented on these two texts in our commentary on the Book of Judges:

4.12.5.en: a. Othniel means "the answering of the Lord," so no one can seize Kirjathsepher (Judg 1:12), that is, enjoy the Holy Bible, except one to whom it is granted by God or whose request is answered; then he marries Achsah the daughter of Caleb, that is, he cleaves to the holy life and comes to know its secrets, not as a village in which he dwells, but as a bride whom he marries[1].

4.12.6.en: b. The choice of Othniel as a judge did not come at random, for God wanted him to be the first of the judges to declare that the secret of victory and salvation lies in God, since the word Othniel means "the answering of God" or "the strength of God"[2]. For salvation is not accomplished by human strength, but by the answer of the Lord, who hears the cries of His children and works in them by His divine power.

4.12.7.en: By him the land had rest forty years; if the land points to the body and the number 40 points to the blessed temporal life, then when we carry within us a soul that walks like this judge by the Spirit of the Lord and enjoys the word of God, our body rests in the Lord, and is holy in His sight all the days of our time. Let Othniel be a leader within us, that we may rest and be filled with surpassing peace!

4.12.8.en: v The Scripture speaks of the savior Othniel, whose name means "the time of the Lord for my benefit." According to this, these first people were delivered from humiliation and bondage by him, and peace returned to the people. The peace which they had lost for a short time in the past because of their pride and their various crimes.

4.12.9.en: It is possible to understand "Chushanrishathaim" in the spiritual sense, as one of the enemies and also "the prince of the power of the air" (Eph 2:2). Therefore it is logical that we follow Othniel, who was raised up from heaven to liberate the people (Lk 2:11). He is (a type) of one of the dwellers of heaven and of the angelic powers, the "ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation" (Heb 1:14). They are the angels of salvation whom Othniel or Ehud represents.

4.12.10.en: Truly the opposing powers fight us, but good divine powers are sent from God to help us.

4.12.11.en: Let us see who Othniel is, and from what noble family. He is the son of Kenaz the brother of Caleb, the wonderful man worthy of praise, who was a companion of Joshua the son of Nun. The Scripture says about Othniel: "And when the children of Israel cried unto the LORD," and "the Spirit of the LORD came upon" Othniel, "and he judged Israel" (Judg 3:9-10)...

4.12.12.en: I do not know whether there is any judge in the Church whom the Lord can consider worthy of being "filled with the Spirit of God" like Othniel himself, who was honored by the testimony of Holy Scripture. These are the leaders whom we desire to be worthy of this testimony. Therefore it says: "And the Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel, and went out to war: and the LORD delivered Chushanrishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand" (Judg 3:10). Why? Because "the Spirit of the LORD" was in him, and also "his hand prevailed against Chushanrishathaim" (Judg 3:10) "And the land had rest forty years." Behold, you see how great is the divine mercy.

4.12.13.en: [For eight years the people of Israel were slaves] (Judg 3:8), because of the sins of many. [And for forty years] (Judg 3:11) they had rest because of the righteousness of one person[3].

4.12.14.en: Origen Seraiah: a Hebrew name meaning "God has prevailed." He is the son of Kenaz and the younger brother of Othniel, and the father of Joab the father of the valley of craftsmen (1 Chr 4:13-14).

4.12.15.en: Hathath: a Hebrew name meaning "terror," a son of Othniel (1 Chr 4:13).

4.13.0.en: And Meonothai begat Ophrah: and Seraiah begat Joab, the father of the valley of craftsmen; for they were craftsmen. [14]

4.13.1.en: Meonothai: a Hebrew name meaning "my dwellings," a man of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 4:14).

4.13.2.en: Ophrah: a Hebrew name meaning "gazelle," the son of Meonothai, of the sons of Judah (1 Chr 4:14).

4.13.3.en: Joab: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh is father," the name of the son of Seraiah, the father of a company of craftsmen (1 Chr 4:14), in the valley of craftsmen, and it may be the "Valley of the Waterfall" that runs to the northwest of Lod toward Joppa.

4.13.4.en: It is observed that the land of Judah was less suitable for agriculture than the land of the northern kingdom, and so we find the proportion of farmers in it small, but we find in it many skilled craftsmen [14], and linen workers [21], and potters [23].

4.13.5.en: We notice that the whole family were craftsmen, skilled in their task, and artisans and merchants. They were creative and diligent above all their neighbors.

4.13.6.en: The father of the valley of craftsmen: that is, the people of the valley of craftsmen (Neh 11:35), which is near Lod, now called Wadi Razia; it was said that the craftsmen of the Temple were from it.

4.14.0.en: And the sons of Caleb the son of Jephunneh; Iru, Elah, and Naam:

4.14.1.en: and the sons of Elah, even Kenaz. [15]

4.14.2.en: Caleb: a Hebrew name meaning "heart," and he is the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite and the elder brother of Othniel. He is one of the twelve spies whom Moses the prophet sent to the Promised Land. Caleb, with Joshua the son of Nun, affirmed the fulfillment of God's promise to the people to take possession of the Promised Land (Num 13-14; Josh 14-15).

4.14.3.en: The majority of the spies (ten spies) stirred up a state of discouragement among the people, while Joshua and Caleb alone held fast to the promise of God, and believed in the power of God and the truthfulness of His promise to His people.

4.14.4.en: In every generation there is a holy remnant, a minority, who believe practically in the promise of God, and bear witness to Him by their lives.

4.14.5.en: Joshua was joined with Caleb in entering the Promised Land; if Jesus – the Lord of glory – is our leader in our entering the Promised Land, then there is no entering it for us unless our heart (Caleb) is earnest and sincere in entering. The joining of Joshua with Caleb is the union of the free divine work with the free human will that accepts the work in the inner depths.

4.14.6.en: In Eshcol Joshua and Caleb carried the one cluster on a pole to enter with it to the people, declaring the fulfillment of the promises of God. It is as though the life-giving Cross is carried by "Jesus" Christ our Lord and carried by the believer with a heart (Caleb) filled with sincerity. It is the Cross of Jesus Christ the Savior, which the believer carries as a fellowship of sufferings with his Lord, to enter with Him into the power of His resurrection.

4.14.7.en: St. John Chrysostom sees in this cluster a pledge of the heavenly life, saying: [Let us not despise heaven!... For He brought to us fruits from heaven, not a cluster of grapes carried on a staff, but "the earnest of the Spirit" (2 Cor 1:22), and citizenship in heaven (Phil 3:20), the things that Paul and the whole company of the Apostles, the wonderful vinedressers, taught us. It was not Caleb the son of Jephunneh nor Joshua the son of Nun who brought these fruits, but Jesus the Son of the [Father of mercies] (2 Cor 1:3), the Son of God who brings every virtue, and brings from heaven all its fruits, that is, its praises![4]]

4.14.8.en: St. Ambrose praised the two spies, for they preferred to speak the truth even if the price was their stoning (Num 14:10), rather than do as the rest of the spies who pleased the people at the expense of the truth. The Saint says: [They preferred to be stoned, as the people threatened them, rather than retreat from their steadfastness full of virtue[5].], [The two good men preferred (divine) glory to safety, but the wicked preferred safety to virtue[6].]

4.14.9.en: Iru: a Hebrew name meaning "cautious." He was the eldest son of Caleb the son of Jephunneh. His name appears as Ir in the Greek Septuagint and in the Vulgate.

4.14.10.en: Elah: a Hebrew name meaning "oak tree," and the name of a son of Caleb of the tribe of Judah is mentioned (1 Chr 4:15). He is distinct from Kenaz mentioned in [13]. The name Kenaz was beloved among the Kenezites.

4.14.11.en: Naam: a Hebrew name meaning "delight." He is a son of Caleb, head of a tribe. His descendants dwelt east of the Jordan.

4.14.12.en: Kenaz: a Semitic name, perhaps meaning "hunting," and it is the name of a son of Elah the son of Caleb.

4.15.0.en: And the sons of Jehaleleel; Ziph, and Ziphah, Tiria, and Asareel. [16]

4.16.0.en: And the sons of Ezra were, Jether, and Mered, and Epher, and Jalon:

4.16.1.en: and she bare Miriam, and Shammai, and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa. [17]

4.16.2.en: Ezra: a Hebrew name meaning "help," of the sons of Judah.

4.16.4.en: Mered: a Hebrew name meaning "rebellion," and he is the son of Ezra and the husband of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh.

4.16.5.en: Epher or Ephar: a Hebrew name meaning "young gazelle," of the line of Ezra.

4.16.6.en: Jalon: a son of Ezra, recorded with the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 4:17).

4.17.0.en: Miriam: of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 4:17). The mother of this Miriam was not mentioned previously, and perhaps she is Bithiah mentioned at the end of [18].

4.17.1.en: Ishbah: a Hebrew name meaning "he praises." He is an ancestor of the inhabitants of Eshtemoa (1 Chr 4:17).

4.18.0.en: (And his wife Jehudijah bare Jered the father of Gedor, and Heber the father of Socho, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah).

4.18.1.en: And these are the sons of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh, which Mered took. [18]

4.18.2.en: And his wife Jehudijah: it is thought that her husband is Mered [18], and it is thought that Bithiah was Egyptian, and a second wife of Mered. Her husband was one of the chiefs of Judah. The meaning of Bithiah is "daughter of the Lord"; perhaps she took this name when she became a Jewess, and her children are Miriam and Shammai and Ishbah, mentioned at the end of [17].

4.18.3.en: Jered or Jarad: a Semitic name, perhaps meaning "descent" or "rose," and he is of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 4:18).

4.18.4.en: Heber: a Hebrew name meaning "fellowship, partner." Of the descendants of Ezra, and the father of the people of Socho.

4.18.6.en: Jekuthiel: a Hebrew name meaning "God nourishes." He is the father of the inhabitants of Zanoah.

4.18.7.en: Zanoah: a Hebrew name meaning "marsh" or "thicket."

4.18.8.en: Bithiah: her name is Hebrew, meaning "daughter of Yahweh" or "worshiper of Yahweh," one of the few women whose names are mentioned in these genealogies. She was the daughter of Pharaoh, and the wife of Mered, a man of Judah. It is likely that she entered the worship of Yahweh with the chosen people.

4.18.9.en: Mered: a Hebrew name meaning "rebellion," son of Ezra of the tribe of Judah, and husband of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh.

4.19.0.en: And the sons of his wife Hodiah the sister of Naham, the father of Keilah the Garmite, and Eshtemoa the Maachathite. [19]

4.19.1.en: Naham: a Hebrew name meaning "consolation," a Jewish man, who married Hodiah his sister (1 Chr 4:19).

4.19.2.en: Keilah the Garmite: he is mentioned in the genealogies of the descendants of Caleb the son of Jephunneh.

4.19.3.en: Eshtemoa: a Hebrew name meaning "obedience." He is Eshtemoa the Maachathite, the son of Ishbah of the tribe of Judah.

4.20.0.en: And the sons of Shimon were, Amnon, and Rinnah the son of Hanan, and Tilon.

4.20.1.en: And the sons of Ishi were, Zoheth, and Benzoheth. [20]

4.20.2.en: Amnon: a Hebrew name meaning "faithful," the son of Shimon of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 4:20).

4.20.3.en: Rinnah the son of Hanan: a Hebrew name meaning "cry of joy," and he is a man from among Judah, the son of Shimon.

4.20.4.en: Tilon: a Hebrew name meaning "lofty." He was the son of Shimon, a man of the descendants of Judah.

4.20.5.en: Ishi: a Hebrew name meaning "savior." There are two with the same name: 1. A man of Judah, the father of Zoheth. 2. A Simeonite whose sons became the head of a band, and attacked the Amalekites in Mount Seir, and seized their settlement and dwelt in it (1 Chr 4:42).

4.20.6.en: Zoheth: a Hebrew name meaning "proud." He is the son of Ishi of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 4:20).

4.20.7.en: Benzoheth: a Hebrew name meaning "son of Zoheth," and he is of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 4:20).

4.21.0.en: The sons of Shelah the son of Judah were, Er the father of Lecah, and Laadah the father of Mareshah, and the families of the house of them that wrought fine linen, of the house of Ashbea, [21]

4.21.1.en: Shelah: a Hebrew name meaning "dog," and he was the third of the sons of Judah (1 Chr 4:21).

4.21.2.en: Er: a Hebrew name meaning "cautious," and he is the son of Shelah, of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 4:21); Shelah had a brother with the same name "Er" (1 Chr 2:3).

4.21.3.en: Lecah: a village in Judah, as may be inferred from the verse (1 Chr 4:21); its location is not known exactly.

4.21.4.en: Laadah: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "thick-necked." (See al-laghd in Arabic, which is the flesh in the throat and around the lower chin to the ear.) Of the family of Shelah, and the father of the inhabitants of Mareshah (1 Chr 4:21).

4.21.5.en: Mareshah: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "place of the head and the summit."

4.21.6.en: Ashbea: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "abundance" or "satiety." Of the descendants of Shelah. His family wove a fine, excellent kind of linen known as bazz. Some think that the house of Ashbea is the name of some place.

4.22.0.en: And Jokim, and the men of Chozeba, and Joash, and Saraph, who had the dominion in Moab, and Jashubilehem.

4.22.2.en: Jokim: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh establishes," one of the sons of Shelah of Judah (1 Chr 4:22).

4.22.3.en: The men of Chozeba: a Hebrew name meaning "lying," a village in Judah inhabited especially by the sons of Shelah (1 Chr 4:22). Most thought it is Chezib or Achzib.

4.22.4.en: Joash: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has given," an abbreviation of Jehoash, a man of the descendants of Judah.

4.22.5.en: Saraph: a Hebrew name meaning "burning or serpent," of the descendants of Shelah, and he was of those who had dominion in Moab.

4.22.6.en: Jashubilehem: a Hebrew name meaning "he returns the bread," most probably the name of a person of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 4:22). But some translations consider the two words not a name but a phrase meaning (and they returned to Lehem).

4.23.0.en: These were the potters and the inhabitants of Netaim and Gederah:

4.23.1.en: there they dwelt with the king for his work. [23]

4.23.2.en: Netaim: a Hebrew name meaning "plantings," a place in Judah where the plantings of the king were.

4.23.3.en: Gederah or Gederi: a Hebrew name meaning "sheepfold." They dwelt in the king's possessions to serve him. They were not among those of great deeds, but gained their fame and honor because they "dwelt... with the king for his work."

4.23.4.en: The secret of the believer's strength, success and honor is to cleave to the King of kings and work for the sake of His Kingdom. Each of them has his gift, but what binds them together is their dwelling with the King to work in His vineyard. For on the Day of the Lord we shall enjoy the heavenly crown, not for the kind of work or service we practiced, but for our faithfulness, and we shall hear His divine voice: "thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things" (Mt 25:21). We shall find children reckoned as heroes, and people of fame scarcely saved as by fire. The reckonings of God rest on the extent of the believer's faithfulness and sincerity, not on his role in the work.

4.24.s.en: 2. The genealogies of the sons of Simeon

4.24.0.en: 24 The sons of Simeon were, Nemuel, and Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul: 25 Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, Mishma his son. 26 And the sons of Mishma; Hamuel his son, Zacchur his son, Shimei his son. 27 And Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters; but his brethren had not many children, neither did all their family multiply, like to the children of Judah. 28 And they dwelt at Beersheba, and Moladah, and Hazarshual, 29 And at Bilhah, and at Ezem, and at Tolad, 30 And at Bethuel, and at Hormah, and at Ziklag, 31 And at Bethmarcaboth, and Hazarsusim, and at Bethbirei, and at Shaaraim. These were their cities unto the reign of David. 32 And their villages were, Etam, and Ain, Rimmon, and Tochen, and Ashan, five cities: 33 And all their villages that were round about the same cities, unto Baal. These were their habitations, and their genealogy. 34 And Meshobab, and Jamlech, and Joshah, the son of Amaziah, 35 And Joel, and Jehu the son of Joshibiah, the son of Seraiah, the son of Asiel, 36 And Elioenai, and Jaakobah, and Jeshohaiah, and Asaiah, and Adiel, and Jesimiel, and Benaiah, 37 And Ziza the son of Shiphi, the son of Allon, the son of Jedaiah, the son of Shimri, the son of Shemaiah; 38 These mentioned by their names were princes in their families: and the house of their fathers increased greatly, 39 And they went to the entrance of Gedor, even unto the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks. 40 And they found fat pasture and good, and the land was wide, and quiet, and peaceable; for they of Ham had dwelt there of old. 41 And these written by name came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and smote their tents and the Meunim that were found there, and destroyed them utterly unto this day, and dwelt in their rooms: because there was pasture there for their flocks. 42 And some of them, even of the sons of Simeon, five hundred men, went to mount Seir, having for their captains Pelatiah, and Neariah, and Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi. 43 And they smote the rest of the Amalekites that were escaped, and dwelt there unto this day.

4.24.1.en: The genealogies of the sons of Simeon were recorded immediately after Judah, perhaps because of the clinging of his tribe to the tribe of Judah. The portion of the tribe of Simeon in the Promised Land was within the borders of the region of Judah (Josh 19:9). In any case, the tribe asked for additional land during the battles.

4.24.2.en: If the tribe of Benjamin joined the tribe of Judah when the schism occurred, many of the Levites were driven out of the northern kingdom and joined the southern kingdom (Judah), and also some of the godly of the tribes left the northern kingdom and joined Judah. Some see that many of the tribe of Simeon joined the land of Judah, especially since their portion in the Promised Land was near the land of Judah.

4.24.3.en: The sons of Simeon were, Nemuel, and Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul: [24]

4.24.4.en: The lands of the tribes of Reuben and Simeon lie in the south, therefore the two tribes were occupied with the political life of Judah, and the lists of the genealogies of the sons of Simeon came right after the kingdom of Judah.

4.25.0.en: Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, Mishma his son. [25]

4.25.1.en: Shallum or Shallumi: a Hebrew name meaning "in peace."

4.25.2.en: Mishma: a Hebrew name meaning "report," the name of a son of Simeon (1 Chr 4:25).

4.25.3.en: Mibsam: a Hebrew name meaning "sweet fragrance," a son of Simeon (1 Chr 4:25).

4.26.0.en: And the sons of Mishma; Hamuel his son, Zacchur his son, Shimei his son. [26]

4.26.1.en: Hamuel: a Hebrew name meaning "zeal of God or wrath of God." He was a Simeonite, a son of Mishma, and perhaps of the family of Shaul (1 Chr 4:26).

4.26.2.en: Zacchur: a Hebrew name meaning "remembering, attentive." He is a Simeonite who came in the line of Mishma.

4.27.0.en: Shimei: (with a kasra on the ayn), a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh hears," he is a Simeonite, who had 16 sons and 6 daughters (1 Chr 4:26-27).

4.27.1.en: And Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters;

4.27.2.en: but his brethren had not many children, neither did all their family multiply, like to the children of Judah. [27]

4.28.0.en: And they dwelt at Beersheba, and Moladah, and Hazarshual, [28]

4.28.1.en: Simeon was small in number; their number at the Exodus was 59,300 (Num 1:23), and after forty years they became only 22,200 (Num 26:14).

4.28.2.en: Moladah: a Hebrew name meaning "birth," inhabited by Shimei of the descendants of Simeon (1 Chr 4:28).

4.29.0.en: And at Bilhah, and at Ezem, and at Tolad, [29]

4.29.1.en: Ezem or Azem: a Hebrew name meaning "great." It is a village near the border of Edom, from the portion of the sons of Judah, which became part of the portion of Simeon. Perhaps it was Khirbet "Umm al-Azm."

4.29.2.en: Bilhah: a Hebrew name meaning "foolish or naive," and it is the name of a place in Simeon.

4.29.3.en: Tolad: a Hebrew name meaning "birth," and it is a city in the south of Judah.

4.30.0.en: And at Bethuel, and at Hormah, and at Ziklag, [30]

4.30.1.en: Hormah: a Hebrew name meaning "devoted place or ruin," and the city of Zephath was called Hormah after its destruction. The Simeonites dwelt in it after it was destroyed.

4.30.2.en: Ziklag: a city in the extreme south of Judah, which was given after a time to Simeon.

4.30.3.en: Bethuel: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "house of God." The name of a place that was in the portion of Simeon.

4.31.0.en: And at Bethmarcaboth, and Hazarsusim, and at Bethbirei, and at Shaaraim.

4.31.1.en: These were their cities unto the reign of David. [31]

4.31.2.en: Susim: plural of Hazar-susah, a Hebrew name meaning "village of horses." It is a village of the Simeonites. Some thought that its place was the stables of Abu Susin, near Tell al-Fari'a, and it may be Susiyah, which lies at a distance of two miles north of Eshtemoa.

4.31.3.en: Bethbirei: a Hebrew name meaning "house of my creation," and it is the name of a city in the land of Simeon.

4.31.4.en: Shaaraim: a Hebrew name meaning "two gates," and it is a city in Simeon.

4.32.0.en: And their villages were, Etam, and Ain, Rimmon, and Tochen, and Ashan, five cities: [32]

4.32.1.en: Ain: a city in Judea, in the southern part of Palestine near Rimmon, which was of the portion of Judah, then given to Simeon, then to the Levites. Perhaps it was Umm al-Ramamin, nine miles northeast of Beersheba.

4.32.2.en: Rimmon: a Hebrew name meaning "pomegranate." A city in the south of Judah near Ain.

4.32.3.en: Tochen: a Hebrew name meaning "measure or weight." A city in the possession of the sons of Simeon, whose place is not known now with certainty.

4.32.4.en: Ashan: a Hebrew name meaning "smoke." It is a town on the coast of Judah, afterward granted to Simeon.

4.33.0.en: And all their villages that were round about the same cities, unto Baal.

4.33.1.en: These were their habitations, and their genealogy. [33]

4.34.0.en: And Meshobab, and Jamlech, and Joshah, the son of Amaziah, [34]

4.34.1.en: Meshobab: a Hebrew name meaning "returned," one of the heads of the sons of Simeon who received pasture near the Arabs, from Gedor (1 Chr 4:34-41).

4.34.2.en: Jamlech: a Hebrew name meaning "he reigns," and he is a Simeonite chief.

4.34.3.en: Joshah: he is a Simeonite chief, the son of Amaziah.

4.35.0.en: And Joel, and Jehu the son of Joshibiah, the son of Seraiah, the son of Asiel, [35]

4.35.1.en: Joel: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh is God," and it is the name of a Simeonite chief.

4.35.2.en: Jehu: a Hebrew name meaning "He is Yahweh," and he is of the descendants of Simeon.

4.35.3.en: Seraiah: a Hebrew name meaning "God has prevailed." More than one person bears this name: 1. The son of Kenaz and brother of Othniel, and father of Joab the father of the valley of craftsmen (1 Chr 4:13-14). 2. The grandfather of Jehu, who was of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chr 4:35).

4.35.4.en: Asiel: a Hebrew name meaning "God has made," one of the forefathers of Joel and Jehu, whose names are mentioned in the division and census of the Hebrews (1 Chr 4:35), and he is a "Simeonite."

4.36.0.en: And Elioenai, and Jaakobah, and Jeshohaiah, and Asaiah, and Adiel, and Jesimiel, and Benaiah, [36]

4.36.1.en: Elioenai: a Hebrew name meaning "my eyes are toward Yahweh," the name of a head of a house in the tribe of Simeon.

4.36.2.en: Jaakobah: a Hebrew name meaning "he takes hold of the heel," and he is a Simeonite chief.

4.36.3.en: Jeshohaiah: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "he makes him bow down." He is a Simeonite chief.

4.36.4.en: Asaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has made," and he is a Simeonite chief in the days of King Hezekiah.

4.36.5.en: Adiel: a Hebrew name meaning "ornament of God," and he is a man of the sons of Simeon, of the heads of the clans.

4.36.6.en: Jesimiel: a Hebrew name meaning "God sets up," and he is a chief of the tribe of Simeon.

4.36.7.en: Benaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "whom Yahweh has built," and he is one of the chiefs of the sons of Simeon.

4.37.0.en: And Ziza the son of Shiphi, the son of Allon, the son of Jedaiah, the son of Shimri, the son of Shemaiah; [37]

4.37.1.en: Shiphi: a Hebrew name meaning "abundant." The father of the prince of the Simeonites in the days of Hezekiah.

4.37.2.en: Allon: a Hebrew name meaning "oak," and it is the name of a son of Jedaiah of the tribe of Simeon.

4.37.3.en: Jedaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh does good," a Simeonite from the ancestors of Ziza (1 Chr 4:7).

4.37.4.en: Shimri: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh guards and preserves," and he is a Simeonite.

4.37.5.en: Shemaiah: it means "Yahweh hears," and he is a Simeonite.

4.38.0.en: These mentioned by their names were princes in their families: and the house of their fathers increased greatly, [38]

4.39.0.en: And they went to the entrance of Gedor, even unto the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks. [39]

4.40.0.en: And they found fat pasture and good, and the land was wide, and quiet, and peaceable; for they of Ham had dwelt there of old. [40]

4.40.1.en: Ham: a Hebrew name meaning "protector, that is, hot, or one who protected with protection."

4.41.0.en: And these written by name came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah,

4.41.1.en: and smote their tents and the Meunim that were found there, and destroyed them utterly unto this day, and dwelt in their rooms: because there was pasture there for their flocks. [41]

4.41.2.en: The events recorded here will be clarified in (2 Chr 20).

4.41.3.en: The Meunim: a tribe of Hamitic origin, whom the sons of Simeon smote in the days of Hezekiah.

4.42.0.en: And some of them, even of the sons of Simeon, five hundred men, went to mount Seir, having for their captains Pelatiah, and Neariah, and Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi. [42]

4.42.1.en: Pelatiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has set free," and it is the name of a Simeonite chief. He entered a war in which the tribe of Simeon was victorious over the Amalekites (1 Chr 4:42-43).

4.42.2.en: Neariah: a Hebrew name meaning "bearer of the shield of Yahweh," and he is one of the sons of Simeon, chief of a tribe, who went to Mount Seir to fight the Amalekites in the days of King Hezekiah.

4.42.3.en: Rephaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has healed," and he is a commander of the sons of Simeon, who lived in the days of Hezekiah.

4.42.4.en: Ishi: a Hebrew name meaning "savior." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. A man of Judah, the father of Zoheth (1 Chr 4:20). 2. A Simeonite, whose sons walked at the head of a band, and attacked the Amalekites in Mount Seir, seized their settlement, and dwelt in it.

4.43.0.en: And they smote the rest of the Amalekites that were escaped, and dwelt there unto this day. [43]

4.43.1.en: They smote the Amalekites who had escaped, after Saul had smitten them (1 Sam 14:48; 15:7-8).

4.43.2.en: That I may meet You through the people of God

4.43.3.en: v With every righteous just man or holy woman, I see You manifested, pouring out Your blessings in my depths.

4.43.4.en: With Jabez, who rose above sorrows and so became, through You, more honorable than his brethren, grant me to enjoy meeting You, and to realize that You are the First and the Last in my life.

4.43.5.en: There is no blessing I could possess without You, O Source of happiness.

4.43.6.en: Bless me, that my heart may be enlarged to love the heavenly beings and human beings.

4.43.7.en: Let every heavenly and human being have a place in my heart.

4.43.8.en: I love everyone, and so I become, with You, a lover of mankind!

4.43.9.en: Let Your hand be with me, You work by me and in me and with me!

4.43.10.en: Accompany me all the days of my sojourning, that evil may have no place in me.

4.43.11.en: You grant me authority over the devil and all his powers.

4.43.12.en: v That I may meet You with Othniel, the first of the judges.

4.43.13.en: You kindle my heart with Your Holy Spirit, so I am filled with strength and wisdom, with peace and joy.

4.43.14.en: I will not cease to meet with You for the peace of my brethren.

4.43.15.en: v You give me the spirit of sincere leadership, so pride will not creep into my heart, nor will slackness gain control over me!

4.43.16.en: In You I strive for the victory of my brethren and their peace.

4.43.17.en: With every success of theirs I count myself successful.

4.43.18.en: And with every groan of heart that comes from them my heart groans!

4.43.19.en: I will not rest until the whole world rests in You.

4.43.20.en: When shall I see all humanity as a rejoicing procession, passing over to You and cleaving to You eternally?!

4.43.21.en: v Allow me to cleave to Caleb the son of Jephunneh, to accompany him as I accompany his friend Joshua the son of Nun.

4.43.22.en: I cross over with them, not to spy out the passing Promised Land, but to set out with You and through You to the heavenly Canaan.

4.43.23.en: I taste the sweetness of the heavenly life, and carry with them the unique cluster of grapes on a pole.

4.43.24.en: I carry You, who have become the grape that passes through the winepress alone for my sake.

4.43.25.en: You carried the staff of the Cross, that the Cross might carry You.

4.43.26.en: You accepted the shame and disgrace of the Cross, to pour Your surpassing glory upon my depths.

4.43.27.en: I long to cleave to You as a bride with her bridegroom.

4.43.28.en: The more I cleave to You, the more my heart opens to humanity.

4.43.29.en: I love You with all my heart, as though there were no one in it but You.

4.43.30.en: And lo, I find a place for every person in my depths.

4.43.31.en: When shall I see all humanity, in the day of Your coming, cleaving to You?!

4.43.32.en: Yes, hasten, O Lord, to every heart.

4.43.33.en: Knock upon it with Your wounded hand, and call every soul to receive You within, so that all may become a holy temple for You!
